newsitem.title: GREECE: BASIC DEPO RATE SIGNALS GREEK MONEY STANCE - CBANK.
newsitem.headline: BASIC DEPO RATE SIGNALS GREEK MONEY STANCE - CBANK.

text.p: The stance of Greek monetary policy is indicated by the basic deposit facility rate and the fixed rate on the 14-day deposit tender, both currently at 11.90 percent, a high-level official at the central bank told Reuters.

"The basic rate of the deposit facility and the fixed rate in the central bank's 14-day depo tender signal the stance of monetary policy," the high-level official at the Bank of Greece told Reuters. "Monetary policy remains the same and is tight."
The central bank holds a fixed-rate depo tender for 14-day funds every Wednesday and has introduced a two-tier deposit facility to fine tune interbank liquidity.
Bank of Greece has set the basic rate of its deposit facility at 11.90 percent for sums up to 300 billion drachmas and the floor rate at 9.90 percent.

"The 9.90-11.90 percent band has worked well in the sense of discouraging speculative forex inflows and therefore reducing surplus liquidity that threatened to rekindle inflationary pressures," he said.

"The central bank will stick to its 11.90 percent basic rate for the time being," the official said. "Bank of Greece will cut its basic deposit facility rate when market and general economic conditions are ripe."
The central bank surprised the market last Wednesday by draining about 50 billion drachmas more than the total expiring on the same day at 11.90 percent.
The move helped push short-term interbank rates up to about 11.90-12.00 percent, depressing fixed coupon bond and FRN prices.

Asked if the finance ministry and the central bank differed on interest rate policy, the official said both pillars of economic policy had the same long-term objective of cutting inflation to 2.5 percent or below.

"The central bank's monetary and foreign exchange policy is geared towards long-term price stability," he said. "This should lead to much lower long-term interest rates and make Greek government securities more attractive."

The treasury will auction 100 billion drachmas of 10-year fixed coupon bonds, its first ever, on June 17. It will also re-open bids for 50 billion drachmas each of three-, five- and seven-year fixed coupon bonds on the same day.

"Of course, the finance ministry wants to slash rates on state securities more aggressively to cut interest payments on the public debt and bring down the budget deficit," he said. "It is normal to pursue such a policy if you are a finance minister." --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
